_comment: What changed, for the people running cameras and the people reading the map.
RULES, because an update popup is a thing that gets abused:
* Only entries that change what someone should DO. Not every commit, not
a changelog. If the reader has no action, it does not belong here.
* 'audience' decides who is interrupted: 'owner' = only devices that have
registered a camera, 'all' = everyone. Most updates are 'owner'; a
visitor reading the map should almost never be interrupted at all.
* 'id' must never be reused or renumbered. It is what a device remembers
as seen, so changing one re-shows the popup to everybody.
🚨 SAY WHAT THE MAP ACTUALLY SHOWS. The first version of the entry below
said cameras were 'drawn on the street next to the one they watch'.
Cameras are NEVER drawn on the map - only the watched stretch of road is,
and a camera's own position is never published at all. Wrong copy in a
transparency project is a bug, and this one would have been read by the
exact people who need to trust the privacy claim.

updates.title: Point your camera at the right road
updates.body: Until now nobody was ever asked which way their camera faces, so the map guessed by pointing it due north. That is why some cameras have the wrong stretch of road marked as watched, and their sightings land on a street they never saw. Your camera's own position is never published either way - the map only ever shows the road. Setting the direction takes about ten seconds, and the page tells you which road it landed on.
